newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end up on improved sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end up on improved sentiment.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed marginally higher on Tuesday with sentiment slightly improved after moderate rises over the past two sessions, brokers said.
The B share index gained 0.55 points or 0.38 percent to finish at 145.78 on turnover of HK$62.67 million, compared with Monday's HK$60.61 million.
Market sentiment is being helped by optimism among investors over China's economic outlook for 1997, brokers said.
"It looks like the B share index is getting strong support at the 140-point level and it is likely to trend higher slowly over the medium term," said an analyst with the Shenzhen J&A Securities.
Despite the recent advances, most institutions remained cautious about buying ahead of the forthcoming annual corporate reporting season and the long Chinese lunar new year holiday, brokers said.
The A share index reversed its early gains and closed down 0.95 points or 0.27 percent at 350.21 on turnover of 4.57 billion yuan against the previous session's 5.01 billion yuan.
Changchun High-tech was the worst A share performer and slid 0.79 yuan or 3.17 percent to 24.10 yuan.

Jiangsu-based garment maker Fareast Industrial Stock Co Ltd, which listed 11.25 million A shares in Shenzhen on Tuesday, ended the session at 14.76 yuan against a recent offer price of 5.30 yuan per share.

Computer parts maker Yantai Dongfang Electronics Information Industry Co Ltd, whose 10.30 million A shares and 6.90 million staff shares were floated in Shenzhen on Tuesday, closed the session at 17.24 yuan.
The A shares were offered at 7.88 yuan each last month while the staff shares were issued at 1.60 yuan each in 1993.
On the B share market, watch maker Fiyta climbed HK$0.20 or 3.64 percent to HK$5.70 on volume of 281,480 shares.
Television tube maker SEG followed, rising HK$0.14 or 2.22 percent to HK$6.44 after 496,402 shares changed hands.
Gujing Distillery, the most active counter, edged up HK$0.04 to HK$10.64 on trade of 1.06 million shares due to investor confidence in the company's earnings outlook, brokers said.
Beverage maker Shenbao was the biggest loser and fell HK$0.06 or 1.26 percent to HK$4.70.
